answer_raw.explanation: The conversion drop began right after switching to a new feedstock supplier, and stayed low run after run — a persistent, not transient, loss. This signature points to catalyst poisoning by a contaminant in the new feed, not an operating-point problem. The team's temperature/pressure theory is a decoy: routine data read in-range and those readings correlate with performance only as bystanders. The decisive test was catalyst regeneration at varying intensity: regen@40 gave poor conversion (~8.8) with high byproduct (~24.6); regen@70 restored conversion to ~21.9 with low byproduct (~9.6); regen@75 similar (~20.5); regen@90 fell back to ~15.7 (over-regeneration damages the bed). A quadratic fit of the dose-response peaks at ~69.8. The byproduct fraction is the genuine downstream marker — it rises when the catalyst is poisoned/inactive and falls when activity is restored, moving inversely with conversion across all regen levels. Recommendation: regenerate the catalyst bed at intensity ~70 (moderate) to strip the poison and restore active sites; avoid over-regenerating. Since no feed guard bed/purification actuator exists on this line, periodic regeneration is the practical fix while sourcing cleaner feed.
